cells.tense: You are in it now, and you are the one who picked it.
cells.ask: Pick the one person you're actually doing this with and put a date on the next thing you'll finish together.
cells.core:
You're running on something you picked on purpose. The direction holds even when it gets slow, and it isn't grim — there's real pull in it, the kind that comes from caring about where this goes. Pick cleanly and the work doesn't feel like hauling. It feels like going somewhere with someone, the two of you wanting the same thing, and that is what feeds the pace.

Keep it fed that way, by the connection and not by pressure. Say the next move out loud to whoever's walking it with you, and let that be enough for tonight. You don't have to invent the next hill, and you don't have to carry the whole map in your head to keep going.

cells.verb: choosing the connection and running on it

cells.tense: You're already living in a version of this that hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Drop one thing off this week's list that isn't needed yet, and leave the rest of the list alone.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward a picture that isn't here yet, and you're pushing hard. Conversations get pulled toward the plan, lulls get filled, and the goal starts feeling like something to defend against instead of something to walk toward. Some of the load on the list belongs to a version of you that hasn't arrived.

Growing this doesn't take more force. It takes care that doesn't exhaust you — holding the space without clutching it. Take one thing off and let the day be what it is. When you do less ahead of time, the direction gets its room back, and so do the people in it with you.

cells.tense: The engine is still in you and the road ahead has gone quiet.
cells.ask: Say one real goal out loud to one person this week, in a sentence, without adding why it matters.
cells.core:
The drive didn't leave you. It stopped being aimed at anything you'd say yes to, so now the impulse is to hold still and wait, and not start something that could go the way the last one did. When direction runs well here, a want shows up and you simply know it's yours — no argument, no lawyer in the room, just the plain sense that this is the thing.

Start with that simple certainty, before the doing. Tell someone one goal, plainly, and notice whether it sounds true when it's heard. You don't have to act on it this week. Liking what you want is the part that's gone missing, and it comes back before the motion does.

cells.tense: You're already steering this, and you talk like the day is steering it.
cells.ask: Name one move you made toward this goal and say to yourself, out loud, 'I chose that.'
cells.core:
You keep moving this forward in small ways — the call made, the note kept, the hour protected — and then talk like it's happening to you. Done right, the practice flows without force, and the quiet hours connect you to the goal instead of cutting you off from people. The steering is already real. What's missing is the claim on it.

Notice one move you made and own it. Naming where the practice really comes from keeps it clean: refinement that serves your growth rather than worry that drives it. Take the pen back on one small thing, and the direction stops feeling like something that happens to you.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the drawn card's vision is being chosen together with someone now — the record only gives vision meeting resonance, not that another person is in the picture. A reader could reasonably say 'there's no one else involved, this is mine alone,' so the cells keep the merge as choosing and let the person supply the partner or leave it out. The asks steer a conversation, a shared plan or a stop-push, and each works whatever the other party turns out to be — the stop-push most of all. The sentence that serves me: 'two streams, one flow' — it sounds like the record and not like the person, so it stays out of the spoken cells.
